Published online:
September 4, 2026

Geographic focus:
India (South Asia), with secondary references to Indonesia, Malaysia, Argentina, Russia, Ukraine, Myanmar, Australia, Canada, and African countries

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [YES] — covers June–August monsoon performance and existing deficits
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — September rainfall outlook, crop yield risks, sugar crushing season starting next month, RBI policy implications near-term
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — winter crop planting cycle (wheat, rapeseed, chickpeas), next sugar cane season, structural inflation pressure, rupee and foreign investment trends

Synopsis:
India's 2026 monsoon is tracking as potentially the weakest in nearly two decades. June started 35% below normal, August ran a deficit, and September is forecast below-average with above-normal temperatures amid El Niño strengthening. Key summer crops — cotton, soybean, corn, rice — entered critical growth stages under moisture stress. Downstream risks include reduced sugar output (forcing imports beyond 1Mt already allowed duty-free), lower vegetable oil production (boosting import demand from multiple origins), weaker pulses output, and potential cotton supply shortfalls. Food inflation already at 5.52% in July with retail CPI at 4.45%, complicating RBI's policy stance. Iran conflict adds a commodity cost overlay. The rupee and foreign investment sentiment are cited as secondary pressure points.
